Generally speaking, an S-loop is a wire-bond loop profile with a longer, relatively flat mid-section between the rise after the first bond and the descent to the second bond. It is used when the span is long, when loop height must stay controlled, when the wire needs extra stiffness against mold sweep, or when clearance over neighboring structures is required.

Author: namibj
Content: so one major reason for the large fan out currently is that we don't know the alignment of the die to the PCB traces with enough precision

Author: namibj
Content: therefore, we need fairly large PCB side landing pads for the bonds

Author: namibj
Content: (much larger than the PCB litho feature size it would reliably offer)

Author: namibj
Content: this causes much longer bonds than would be needed otuwise due to limited bond density on the PCB side

Author: namibj
Content: Notably, compare the bond pad landing site size to how narrow the escape tracks at the bottom are

Author: namibj
Content: The PCB litho could do almost double the density if the alignment would be better
